description: Persist CircuitBreaker state to the database (the KillSwitch persistence already exists in persistent_kill_switch.py). Create a CircuitBreakerRecord model, a PersistentCircuitBreaker class, and integrate the kill switch DB loading into the app lifespan. Also wire the persistent kill switch load_active() call into the FastAPI lifespan handler so active kill switches are loaded from DB on startup.
steps: Create src/nexus/governance/circuit_breaker_model.py with CircuitBreakerRecord(SQLModel, table=True). Fields: id (UUID PK), agent_id (UUID, indexed), consecutive_failures (int), is_open (bool), last_failure_at (datetime | None), opened_at (datetime | None), cooldown_seconds (int, default=300), updated_at (datetime).

Create src/nexus/governance/persistent_circuit_breaker.py with PersistentCircuitBreaker class (mirrors the pattern in persistent_kill_switch.py). Methods: record_failure(agent_id) -> bool (returns True if circuit just opened), record_success(agent_id) -> None, is_open(agent_id) -> bool, reset(agent_id) -> None, load_state() -> dict[UUID, CircuitBreakerState] (load all open circuits from DB). Takes async_sessionmaker in __init__.
Import CircuitBreakerRecord in src/nexus/models/__init__.py so Alembic discovers it.

In src/nexus/main.py lifespan handler, after the SQLite table creation and seeding, add: (a) instantiate PersistentKillSwitch with async_session_factory, call await persistent_ks.load_active(), (b) log that governance state was loaded from DB. Import PersistentKillSwitch from nexus.governance.persistent_kill_switch.

Add tests in tests/test_persistent_circuit_breaker.py covering: record_failure increments count, record_failure opens circuit at threshold, record_success resets count, is_open returns correct state. Use AsyncMock for the session factory following the pattern in tests/conftest.py.
acceptance_criteria: The app lifespan in main.py calls PersistentKillSwitch.load_active() on startup
Running 'python -m pytest tests/test_persistent_circuit_breaker.py -v' passes all new tests
Running 'python -m pytest tests/ --tb=short -q' still passes all existing tests
findings: All 739 tests pass (726 existing + 13 new). Used datetime.utcnow() to match existing project patterns (kill_switch_model.py, persistent_kill_switch.py). The lifespan block gracefully handles missing DB tables with a try/except.
